purpose: Methods, stopping gates, anti-busywork protections, and reporting constraints should be typed separately from atomic intentions.

candidates.meaning: One task finishes; this alone is not a general stop condition.
A checkpoint is reached; its meaning depends on the requested handoff policy.
One local blocker does not imply all other authorized work is blocked.
Other in-scope work can be advanced while a requirement is blocked.
Original agreed scope is satisfied with evidence; do not invent follow-on work.
Remaining requirements cannot advance with available tools and permissions.
External execution/time/tool limit prevents further work in this interaction.

design_constraints: Treat isolated blockers differently from global inability to progress.
An unavailable runtime is not proof of user-requested completion.
Verification and progress percentage depend on established measurable acceptance criteria.
Do not automatically add behavior to the prompt text from descriptive metadata.
Use proportionate process checks, minimizing instruction overload.
open_review_questions: Which conditions are independent ontological classes versus facets of an execution contract?
How can conflicting handoff constraints be surfaced without enforcing them automatically?
